items.title: Implement backlog-root.ts resolution functions with unit tests and shared test helper
items.description:
Replace the placeholder stubs in `packages/core/src/backlog-root.ts` with full implementations, create the shared test helper, and write comprehensive unit tests.

1. Implement `resolveBacklogRoot(projectPath, backlogFlag?)` in `packages/core/src/backlog-root.ts`:
   - No flag → return `ok(path.join(path.resolve(projectPath), ".ralph"))`
   - With flag → resolve relative to projectPath, validate sandboxing via `validatePath()` from `./fs-utils.js`
   - Return `PATH_VIOLATION` error if outside project root
   - Import `validatePath` from `./fs-utils.js` and `Result, ok, err, ErrorCodes` from `./errors.js`

2. Implement `resolveStateDir(backlogRoot)` — pure function:
   - `path.basename(resolved) === ".ralph"` → return resolved (no nesting)
   - Otherwise → return `path.join(resolved, ".ralph")`

3. Implement `resolveBacklogPaths(projectPath, backlogRoot)` — returns `Result<BacklogPaths>`:
   - Validate backlogRoot within projectPath
   - Check backlogRoot directory exists
   - Locate backlog.json: check root first, then stateDir fallback
   - Build full BacklogPaths object per spec 02 section 2.3
   - Use `fileExists()` from `./fs-utils.js` for existence checks

4. Implement `resolveInstructionPaths(paths)` — synchronous:
   - Check `{stateDir}/RALPH.md` first, fallback to `{projectPath}/.ralph/RALPH.md`
   - Same for REVIEW.md
   - Return null if neither exists
   - Skip fallback when stateDir === projectRalphDir (default root case)

5. Implement `ensureStateDir(paths)` — delegates to `ensureDir(paths.stateDir)` from `./fs-utils.js`

6. Create `packages/core/src/test-helpers.ts` with `createMultiRootProject()` function per spec 07 section 2. This file must NOT be exported from the barrel.

7. Create `packages/core/src/backlog-root.test.ts` with tests covering:
   - resolveBacklogRoot: no flag default, custom path, path traversal rejection, empty string
   - resolveStateDir: .ralph basename, custom basename
   - resolveBacklogPaths: backlog.json in root, in stateDir, missing, nonexistent dir, all paths absolute
   - resolveInstructionPaths: per-root RALPH.md, project-level fallback, missing everywhere, default root
   - ensureStateDir: creates dir with parents, existing dir no-op
acceptanceCriteria: resolveBacklogRoot with no flag returns {projectPath}/.ralph
resolveBacklogRoot with '../../outside' returns PATH_VIOLATION error
resolveStateDir for .ralph basename returns same directory (no nesting)
resolveStateDir for specs/auth returns specs/auth/.ralph
resolveBacklogPaths finds backlog.json in root directory first
resolveBacklogPaths falls back to stateDir for backlog.json
resolveBacklogPaths returns FILE_NOT_FOUND when no backlog.json exists
resolveInstructionPaths finds per-root RALPH.md when present
resolveInstructionPaths falls back to project-level RALPH.md
test-helpers.ts is NOT exported from packages/core/src/index.ts

items.title: Implement lock.ts lock file management with unit tests
items.description:
Replace the placeholder stubs in `packages/core/src/lock.ts` with full implementations and write unit tests.

1. Implement helper functions in `packages/core/src/lock.ts`:
   - `isProcessAlive(pid)` — uses `process.kill(pid, 0)` in try/catch
   - `isProcessRecycled(pid, recordedStartTime)` — reads `/proc/{pid}/stat` on Linux, returns false on non-Linux
   - `getProcessStartTime(pid)` — reads `/proc/{pid}/stat` field 22, returns null on non-Linux
   - For `/proc/{pid}/stat` parsing: find last `)`, split remainder, field 22 is at index 19 in post-paren fields

2. Implement `acquireLock(paths)` in lock.ts:
   - Call checkLock first
   - If locked && !stale → return LOCK_CONFLICT error with pid, startedAt, and relative path in message
   - If locked && stale → remove stale lock file
   - Write new lock with `atomicWrite(paths.lock, ...)` containing pid, startedAt, processStartTime
   - Import `atomicWrite` and `fileExists` from `./fs-utils.js`

3. Implement `releaseLock(paths)` — fs.unlinkSync with ENOENT tolerance (idempotent)

4. Implement `checkLock(paths)` — read lock file, validate with LockFileContentSchema, check PID liveness and recycling

5. Implement `forceClearLock(paths)` — delegates to releaseLock

6. Create `packages/core/src/lock.test.ts` with tests:
   - acquireLock on fresh dir creates .loop.lock with valid JSON
   - acquireLock when locked by current (live) PID returns LOCK_CONFLICT
   - acquireLock when locked by dead PID (use PID 999999999) removes stale lock and acquires
   - acquireLock with corrupt lock file treats as stale
   - releaseLock removes lock file
   - releaseLock returns ok when no lock exists
   - checkLock returns { locked: false } when no lock
   - checkLock returns { locked: true, stale: false } for live PID
   - checkLock returns { locked: true, stale: true } for dead PID
   - forceClearLock removes lock regardless
acceptanceCriteria: acquireLock creates .loop.lock with pid, startedAt, and processStartTime fields
acquireLock returns LOCK_CONFLICT when locked by a live process
acquireLock removes stale lock (dead PID) and acquires successfully
releaseLock removes .loop.lock file
releaseLock returns ok even when no lock file exists (idempotent)
checkLock returns { locked: false } when no lock file
checkLock returns stale: true for dead PID
forceClearLock removes lock regardless of PID status
Lock file JSON validates against LockFileContentSchema
pnpm typecheck passes
pnpm test packages/core/src/lock.test.ts passes
items.notes: Read spec 03-lock-file-management.md completely — it has exact implementation logic including the /proc/{pid}/stat parsing algorithm. Use process.pid for 'live PID' tests and 999999999 for 'dead PID' tests. The lock file path comes from paths.lock (set by resolveBacklogPaths). Use createMultiRootProject from test-helpers.ts (import via relative path '../test-helpers.js', NOT from barrel). The relative path in LOCK_CONFLICT error messages uses path.relative(paths.projectPath, paths.root).

items.title: Loop runner's `git add -A` commits transient runtime state into git history
items.description: The loop runner commits via `git add -A && git commit` (packages/loop/src/git-commit.ts), which sweeps its OWN runtime files into the per-item commit: .loop.lock (a lock file!), state.json, backlog.json.bak, and the DONE marker. Observed during the release-automation loop (commit 62190f2 contained .rauf/.loop.lock + state.json + backlog.json.bak). Lock/marker files must never enter history. Fix: gitignore the per-backlog .rauf/ runtime files (lock, state.json, *.bak, DONE, rauf.log) and/or scope the runner's staging to exclude its own state dir via pathspec. NOTE: the agent-self-commit half of this was already fixed live in .rauf/RAUF.md (commit 656d8c6); this item is the runner-side staging hygiene follow-up.

items.title: Single-gate review for loops — suppress per-iteration security/review hooks in child sessions
items.description: When a commit/Stop-triggered review hook (e.g. the security-guidance plugin) is installed globally, the loop's child agent sessions trigger it every iteration. With the agent self-commit removed (RAUF.md 656d8c6) the heavyweight commit-review no longer fires, but the Stop-hook diff review still runs per child session, and there is no first-class way to run a loop with per-iteration review hooks suppressed in favor of ONE review over the cumulative branch diff. For human-in-the-loop autonomous dev, per-item review inside autonomous child sessions is the wrong altitude (the agent rubber-stamps findings); review belongs at the gate, surfaced to the human. Add: a documented/opt-in way for the loop to spawn child sessions with per-iteration review hooks disabled (e.g. propagate ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0 or a generic hook-suppression env), plus a post-loop gate review over main..HEAD.
acceptanceCriteria: Loop provides a documented, opt-in flag/config to run child sessions without per-iteration review-hook noise
A single review over the cumulative branch diff (main..HEAD) is run or documented as the gate step after the loop

Default behavior is unchanged unless explicitly opted in

items.notes: Surfaced while dogfooding forge-5-loop on release-automation, 2026-06-10. The harness auto-mode classifier also blocks ad-hoc ENABLE_CODE_SECURITY_REVIEW=0 on the loop command, reinforcing the need for a first-class, intentional mechanism.
